name: cairn-builtin-java
description: Built-in Java registry pack bundled with the Cairn reference compiler. The block tables, each block's state properties and their values, and each targetable version's DataVersion are extracted from the game by `.github/scripts/extract_registry.py`: each version's server jar runs its data generator with `--reports`, and `extracted` names the jar each table came from. The `connections` table is extracted too, from each version's block tags in its server jar and the block models its client jar ships, and `extracted` names both jars. The `aliases` groups are hand-written: the spellings one block has worn, so a refused id can be answered with the name this target does use. They cover the Java/Bedrock spelling splits an author most often walks into and the ids Bedrock's own 1.21.40 flattening wave retired. Two cases are deliberately absent. A spelling both editions declare meaning different blocks (`snow` is Java's snow layer and Bedrock's snow block) gets no row, because a group is keyed on the spelling alone and the two pairs would have to share one. The seven numbered pre-flattening slab ids (`stone_block_slab2` … `4`, `double_stone_block_slab` … `4`) are absent for a different reason: each carried several unrelated materials in one state value and the 1.21.40 wave scattered them across the edition's 124 slab ids, and which of those each old id covers is recorded in no table shipped here — the row would be a guess. That is what separates them from the state-split families that are included (`stonebrick`, `monster_egg`, `skull`): each of those splits into one family, and the whole family is the answer. The `absent` list is hand-written too: the Bedrock blocks Java has no counterpart for, each with the reason, so that a Java build that names one says the block is Bedrock's rather than unknown. A block Java spells another way is a rename and belongs in `aliases`, so the list holds only blocks Java lacks under every spelling: Bedrock's world-building blocks, its Education Edition blocks and chemistry, its item-frame blocks, and the Nether reactor of the old Pocket Edition.
